Solid-State Batteries: Technology Overview

Published 2026-03-12 by the Fixture Energy Institute.

Solid-state batteries replace the liquid electrolyte of conventional lithium-ion cells with a solid conductor, eliminating the most common cause of thermal runaway.

Key results

  • The Zephyr-7 prototype cell achieved an energy density of 412 Wh/kg in March 2026 testing.
  • The Zephyr-7 retained 91% of its capacity after 1,200 charge cycles, versus roughly 78% for the comparison lithium-ion pack.
  • Charging from 10% to 80% took 14 minutes at 4C.

Remaining obstacles

The main manufacturing obstacle is dendrite formation at the lithium-metal anode interface, which current sintering processes only suppress below 45°C. Production yield at the pilot line is 62%, well short of the 95% needed for automotive pricing.
